content: To create a proper MLA Works Cited page, follow these detailed steps: 1. Title the Page: At the top of the page, center the title Works Cited. Do not italicize, bold, or underline the title. 2. Margins and Spacing: Use one-inch margins on all sides of the page. The entire Works Cited page should be double-spaced, with no extra spaces between entries. 3. Alphabetical Order: Arrange all entries alphabetically by the last name of the author. If no author is available, alphabetize by the title of the work, ignoring articles like A, An, or The. 4. Hanging Indent: Each entry should use a hanging indent. This means the first line of each citation is flush with the left margin, and subsequent lines are indented by 0.5 inches. 5. Formatting Authors: For a single author, list the last name first, followed by a comma and the first name. For multiple authors, list the first author in the same format, followed by the other authors in standard order (first name followed by last name). Use et al. for works with more than three authors. 6. Titles of Works: Italicize the titles of books, journals, and other standalone works. Use quotation marks for titles of shorter works, such as articles, essays, or chapters. 7. Publication Information: Include all necessary publication details, such as the publisher, publication year, and volume/issue numbers for journal articles. For online sources, include the URL or DOI, and specify the date of access if required. 8. Abbreviations for Months: When citing dates, abbreviate the names of months (e.g., Jan., Feb., Mar.) except for May, June, and July, which are written in full. 9. No Page Numbers: If a source does not have page numbers, such as many online documents, do not invent or include page numbers. 10. Citing a Work Without an Author: If a work does not have an author, begin the citation with the title of the work. Alphabetize it based on the first significant word of the title. 11. Consistency: The MLA Handbook is the authoritative source for MLA style. 12. Additional Notes: If you consult works that you do not directly cite in your paper, you may include them in a separate section titled Works Consulted, formatted similarly to the Works Cited page. By adhering to these detailed instructions, you can create a precise and professional MLA Works Cited page that meets academic standards.
